The State government on Wednesday awarded direct work orders to eight start-ups under its “Government First Initiative” to build technology solutions for the Praja Seva Department and the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB).
The initiative, announced on the second day of the 29th edition of Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS) 2026 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC), is expected to connect innovators directly with State departments to solve public sector challenges.
Under the programme, each winning start-up is eligible for a direct work order of up to ₹25 lakh. The total committed project value stands at ₹99.78 lakh (inclusive of GST) for the Praja Seva Department, while it is ₹1 crore for the BWSSB.
According to the government, the winners emerged from a competitive pool of 150 applications submitted between October 8 and October 23, 2026, with the Praja Seva receiving 76 entries and the BWSSB receiving 74. The rigorous five-stage selection process included application submission, eligibility screening, selection committee evaluation, discussions with respective department officials, and final budget negotiations. The committee assessed start-ups on innovation, technical soundness, product readiness, scalability, and integration capability.
Four start-ups were selected to modernise citizen services and administrative workflows for the Praja Seva Department and each was awarded ₹25 lakh. These include: SanMejora, to develop an AI-enabled grievance management and redressal system; VTT AI Private Limited, to create an AI-powered unified citizen call centre; Datafrontier Innovations Private Limited, to build an AI-enabled e-Office and unified officer workflow platform and Nife Apps Labs, to ensure the uptime and availability of citizen-facing government IT services.
Another set of four start-ups were chosen across five challenge areas to optimise urban water infrastructure for the BWSSB and these include: Smart Terra, for an AI and digital innovation challenge focused on urban water management and reducing non-revenue water; UniaX Technologies, to deploy an intelligent asset management solution; Krishi Hrudya Private Limited, to implement GIS-enabled revenue and operational intelligence and Calypsion Innovations LLP, to develop a digital twin for integrated water management.
Highlighting the vision behind the programme, Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home and Information Technology & Biotechnology and E-Governance, said, “The initiative reflects our commitment to making government an active partner and customer of Karnataka’s start-up ecosystem. We want to create opportunities for start-ups to take their innovations beyond the proof-of-concept stage and demonstrate their solutions in real-world governance settings.”
Responding to media queries, the Minister said other government departments might also come up with respective problem statements, allowing a large number of start-ups to develop solutions and work with the government.
The Government First Initiative is a pioneering policy by the State government that makes the State the first customer for local start-ups developing technology-driven solutions to public sector and governance challenges.
